12 Which diagram shows a couple?
A

hints: Notice the direction of each arrow labelled $F$ at the ends of the bar in diagrams A to D.
Recall a couple needs two equal forces that are parallel but opposite, giving zero resultant force plus a resultant moment.
Check which diagram has one $F$ up at one end and one $F$ down at the other end with parallel lines of action.
walkthrough: Identify the test: a couple is two forces with same magnitude $F$, parallel lines of action, opposite directions, separated by a distance.
In diagram A the left $F$ acts up and the right $F$ acts down, so the vectors are $+F$ and $-F$ and sum to zero resultant force.
Both forces in A tend to turn the bar the same way about the centre dot, so the moments add and the resultant moment is $F \times$ separation, not zero.
Diagram B has two upward forces giving resultant $2F$, diagram C has non-parallel forces, and diagram D has only one force, so none gives zero resultant with a turning effect.
Only the equal, opposite, parallel pair satisfies the couple definition. This is option A.

A.explanation: Two forces of size $F$ are equal, opposite and parallel with zero resultant but a non-zero turning effect, which is a couple.

B.explanation: Both forces $F$ act upwards in the same direction, so the resultant is $2F$ upwards and not a couple.

C.explanation: The left $F$ is angled while the right $F$ is vertical, so the forces are not parallel and opposite and do not form a couple.

D.explanation: Only one force $F$ acts, so there is a resultant force and it cannot be a pair of equal opposite forces.
